<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro secúndo Machabæórum
<r>2 Mac 8:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Iudas vero Machabǽus, et qui cum illo erant, introíbant laténter in castélla: et convocántes cognátos et amícos, et eos qui permansérunt in Iudaísmo assuméntes, eduxérunt ad se sex míllia virórum.
<n>2</n> Et invocábant Dóminum, ut respíceret in pópulum qui ab ómnibus calcabátur, et misererétur templo quod contaminabátur ab ímpiis:
<n>3</n> Misererétur étiam extermínio civitátis, quæ esset íllico complanánda, et vocem sánguinis ad se clamántis audíret.

<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

b.61be36e94a:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>T</c>értio Kaléndas Novémbris Luna tricésima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>I</h>n Sardínia natális sancti Pontiáni, Papæ et Mártyris, qui, ab Alexándro Imperatóre, una cum Hippólyto Presbýtero, in eam ínsulam deportátus, ibídem, mactátus fústibus, martýrium consummávit. Eius corpus a beáto Fabiáno Papa Romam delátum est, atque in cœmetério Callísti sepúltum. Ipsíus tamen festum recólitur tertiodécimo Kaléndas Decémbris.
<h>Æ</h>géæ, in Cilícia, pássio sanctórum Zenóbii Epíscopi, et Zenóbiæ soróris, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre et Lýsia Prǽside.
<h>A</h>ltíni, in Venetórum fínibus, sancti Theonésti, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui ab Ariánis occísus est.
<h>I</h>n Africa natális sanctórum Mártyrum ducentórum vigínti.
<h>T</h>ingi, in Mauritánia, pássio sancti Marcélli Centuriónis, qui, sanctórum Cláudii ac Lupérci et Victórii Mártyrum pater, cápitis abscissióne martýrium complévit sub Agricoláo, agente vices Præfécti prætório.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sanctórum trédecim Mártyrum, qui, cum sanctis Iuliáno, Euno et Macário, passi sunt sub Décio Imperatóre.
<h>C</h>árali, in Sardínia, sancti Saturníni Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Bárbaro Prǽside, cápite truncátus est.
<h>A</h>paméæ, in Phrýgia, sancti Máximi Mártyris, sub eódem Diocletiáno.
<h>L</h>egióne, in Hispánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Cláudii, Lupérci et Victórii, filiórum sancti Marcélli Centuriónis; qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni et Maximiáni, sub Diogeniáno Prǽside, iussi sunt decollári.
<h>L</h>utétiæ Parisiórum sancti Lucáni Mártyris.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sanctæ Eutrópiæ Mártyris, quæ, Mártyres vísitans, apprehénsa est, et, cum illis sævíssime cruciáta, réddidit spíritum.
<h>A</h>ntiochíæ sancti Serapiónis Epíscopi, eruditióne claríssimi.
<h>C</h>ápuæ sancti Germáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris, magnæ sanctitátis viri; cuius ánimam, in hora óbitus eius, ab Angelis in cælum deférri sanctus Benedíctus aspéxit.
<h>P</h>oténtiæ, in Lucánia, sancti Gerárdi Epíscopi.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.d7e2d954ef:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>O</c>ctober 30th 2027, the 30th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>O</h>n the same day, the holy martyr, Pope Pontian, who was exiled to Sardinia along with the Priest Hippolytus, under the Emperor Alexander, and was there cudgelled to death. His body was brought to Rome by blessed Pope Fabian, and buried in the cemetery of Kallistus.
<h>A</h>t Algaea, in Cilicia, under the President Lysias and the Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyrs Zenobius, Bishop (of that see,) and Zenobia his sister.
<h>A</h>t Altino, the holy martyr Theonestus, Bishop (of Philippi, in Macedonia,) who was slain by the Arians.
<h>I</h>n Africa, two hundred and twenty holy martyrs.
<h>A</h>t Tangiers, in Morocco, (in the third century,) the holy centurion Marcellus, who accomplished martyrdom by being beheaded under Agricolaus, Vicar to the Prefect of the Pretorium.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, thirteen holy martyrs, who suffered under the Emperor Decius, along with Julian, Eunus, and Macarius.
<h>A</h>t Cagliari, in Sardinia, the holy martyr Saturninus, who was beheaded under the President Barbarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.
<h>A</h>t Apamea, in Phrygia, under the same Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyr Maximus.
<h>A</h>t Leon, in Spain, the holy martyrs Claudius, Lupercus, and Victorius, sons of the holy centurion Marcellus, who were beheaded under the President Diogenian, in the persecution under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian.
<h>A</h>t Paris, the holy martyr Lucan.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria also, the holy martyr Eutropia, who visited the martyrs, and, being most cruelly tormented along with them, gave up the ghost.
<h>A</h>t Antioch, (in the third century,) holy Serapion, Patriarch (of that see,) eminent for his learning.
<h>A</h>t Capua, the holy Confessor Germanus, Bishop (of that see,) a man of great holiness, whose soul, at the hour of his death, holy Benedict saw carried heavenward by Angels.
<h>A</h>t Potenza, in Lucania, (in the year 1119,) holy Gerard, Bishop (of that see.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
